technical_and_design_decisions: Target platform is the Spring Cloud Data Flow (s-c-d) server and shell, with Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s) module model for stream modules; all new code follows existing project conventions (Java, Maven/Gradle multi-module builds).

U1: Implement 'runtime info' as a new Spring Shell command in the Data Flow shell that queries a server-side REST endpoint; the endpoint aggregates per-module runtime details (host, port, and similar attributes) from the deployer SPI and renders them as a table in the shell.

U2: Implement YARN support as a Spring Cloud Deployer SPI implementation built on Spring for Apache Hadoop (Spring YARN), communicating with the YARN ResourceManager for stream/task app deployment; deliver a dedicated YARN data flow server distribution that embeds the YARN deployer instead of the local deployer; support cluster configuration and Kerberos security settings.

U3: Port the Spring XD 'file' module to a Spring Cloud Stream source module (Spring Boot application with @EnableBinding on a Source) in the spring-cloud-stream-modules style, reusing XD business logic where feasible and adapting to the s-c-s programming and options model.

U4: Refactor the build into separate modules/profiles so each SPI deployer (local, YARN, etc.) is built and released as an individual artifact; the admin/data flow server resolves the deployer from the classpath rather than bundling all deployer variants into one deliverable.

U5: Replace legacy XDRuntimeException with standard or domain-specific exceptions (e.g., IllegalStateException or dedicated data flow exceptions), preserving error semantics; update all throw sites, catch blocks, and tests.

U6: Upgrade the gemfire sink to the latest stable GemFire release, aligned with the compatible Spring Data GemFire version; resolve API/behavioral changes and re-run integration tests against a live GemFire instance.

U7: Implement the SFTP source on top of the Spring Integration SFTP inbound channel adapter; use an embedded SFTP server (e.g., Apache MINA SSHD) for integration tests; register SFTP as an out-of-the-box module and publish its artifacts to the Spring maven snapshot repository.
U8: Implement CI pipelines (existing CI server, e.g., Jenkins/Concourse) per repository of the Data Flow family, running unit and integration tests on every commit with status notifications.

Existing codebases are available: the data flow server/shell, the spring-cloud-stream-modules repo, and the Spring XD codebase as the source for ports (file module, XDRuntimeException removal).

A CI server with repository access already exists; U8 covers configuring/fixing pipelines, not procuring infrastructure.
Estimates include unit tests, integration tests, and user-facing documentation updates for each story.
